A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Lorentz-space optimization and convolution framework by the same authors. The complete text, equations, tables and figures support comparison, including Appendix A in v2; v1 has no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original metric-learning and classification results, computational measurements, and component ablations in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains original metric-learning, classification and ablation results and adds original VAE reconstruction and generation results in Section 4.3 and Table 4.

M1.justification: The documented scaling coefficient changes from atanh(0.99/(s Dmax)) in v1 Equation 3 to atanh(0.99)/(s m), with m=Dmax, in v2 Equation 2. This changes the prescribed scaling for fixed parameters. The main curvature-update, AdamW, convolution and LHIER designs remain; v2 also presents an equivalent factorized implementation of spatial rescaling.

E1.justification: Section 4.3 adds VAE image reconstruction and generation on CIFAR-100 and CelebA, extending evaluation beyond classification and metric learning into generative modeling and face images. In-Shop results disappear, but its continued inclusion in the experimental description prevents concluding that the dataset itself ceased to be used.

E2.justification: The new VAE comparison evaluates Euclidean, hybrid Poincare VAE by Mathieu et al., hybrid Lorentz VAE by Nagano et al., and fully hyperbolic HCNN by Bdeir et al. against HCNN+. This introduces substantive generative comparators. Comparator membership in the retained metric-learning and classification comparisons is unchanged after matching renamed models.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a distinct VAE evaluation protocol using reconstruction and generation FID, alongside the retained Recall@k and classification-accuracy evaluations. Section 4.3 specifies curvature learning with the adjusted Riemannian SGD scheme for these new experiments. No changes to retained experiments' splits, metrics or model sizes are established.

E4.justification: v2 removes the brief analysis in v1 Section 4.2 reporting that learned encoder curvature approaches approximately -0.6. The component-removal ablations, numerical failure without the optimizer scheme, and 130-versus-200-epoch convergence comparison remain unchanged and move to Appendix A.3.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the same five-run mean and standard-deviation reporting. The added VAE table also reports five-run results with plus/minus values, extending the existing reporting practice rather than introducing a different statistical procedure. No new seed reporting, confidence intervals or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes six LHIER/ResNet-50 values, including CUB R@1 from 71.0 to 72.4 and Cars R@1 from 88.7 to 89.1, and removes all In-Shop result columns. v2 adds VAE FID results and ResNet-18 memory/runtime measurements. Classification accuracies and ablation values are unchanged; the ResNet-50 resource values are retained from v1 Table 4.

T1.justification: v2 adds formal Lorentz-group, rotation and boost definitions and decomposition in Appendix A.1, derives factorized spatial rescaling in Appendix A.2, and states a distance-preservation identity in Section 3.2. It also changes the sign of the manifold constraint in Section 3.1. The parallel-transport and centroid formulas are relocated rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: The conclusion expands the claimed empirical validation from two problem scenarios to three vision tasks, incorporating generation. The abstract and four introduction contributions retain essentially the same scientific claims about curvature learning, normalization, AdamW and efficient convolutions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of GeoOpt stabilization failures, clipping and saturation drawbacks, and compatibility with other curvature-learning methods. It broadens possible explanations for weak transformer results and replaces the classification discussion's learned-curvature explanation with a scaling hypothesis. The conclusion drops the proposed investigation of embedding bounding while retaining batch-normalization and dimensionality-reduction limitations.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that metric-learning hyperparameters were kept at defaults and describes the VAE implementation using efficient convolution, transpose convolution and adjusted Riemannian SGD. However, it omits v1's explicit classification scaling factor s=2 and resource-comparison batch size of 80. These disclosure changes do not establish changed settings or reruns.

R1.justification: v2 adds Mathieu et al., Ovinnikov and Hsu et al. for VAE motivation, and Moretti for Lorentz decomposition. These are focused additions supporting the new material; the main related-work discussion and positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Methodological explanations and experimental discussions undergo substantial rewriting, with a new methodology overview and a shortened conclusion. Background operations and ablations move into a newly organized appendix. The title drops 'Curvature', and citation style, terminology and author-header text also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds tangent-plane and scaling-function figures, retaining the bottleneck diagram as Figure 2. It removes In-Shop columns, adds resource columns to classification tables, incorporates v1's resource table into Table 3, adds the VAE table, and relocates the ablation table. Algorithm boxes and the overall document layout are substantially reformatted.

improvement.justification: Clearer curvature-transport and rescaling explanations, correction of v1's unsupported '74%' accuracy-lift statement, and five-run VAE comparisons improve assessability and support applicability to generation. The net gain is limited by omitted In-Shop results, loss of explicit scaling and batch-size settings, and a norm-versus-squared-norm inconsistency in the new Appendix A.2.
